clue.text: Impotent employing frozen water, it's clear

indicators.note: to employ something is to take it on, so the word for impotent takes the ice into its body

parts.note: split as NOT ABLE, unable to do anything
ice is simply water that has frozen

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a powerless person is using ice, as if that settles a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impotent' must be read as two words meaning unable, and the frozen water goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noticeable is plainly visible, which is one sense of clear, an adjective of obviousness.

clue.text: English gent getting elevated for title

indicators.note: in a down entry, being raised means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: An English gentleman is raised to the peerage and receives a title.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ennoblement; in a down clue 'elevated' means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is what something is called, a synonym for its name.

clue.text: Will try to accept pet name

indicators.note: the word for try takes in the other letters, accepting them inside it

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a pet is a tame animal

explanation.surface: Someone will try to get used to a pet's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' at the start looks like the auxiliary verb; it is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the document setting out a person's bequests.

clue.text: Chase one's neighbour, grinding away initially!

definitions.text: Chase one's neighbour, grinding away initially!

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

parts.note: the five words supply their opening letters in order

explanation.surface: A picture of dancers in a line, each pursuing the person ahead while gyrating.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it: in a conga each dancer follows the one in front, hips grinding.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin-American line dance in which each dancer holds the one in front.

clue.text: Gold colour for good sign

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
spice is a warm orange-brown shade

explanation.surface: A gold colour is taken as a lucky omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen, especially a favourable one, from Roman augury by watching birds.

clue.text: Learning three Rs possibly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: RRR are three characters of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, which suggests schooling, but taken literally they are three R characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means literary learning, and the three Rs are literally alphabetic characters.

clue.text: Get prince occasionally to be heroic

indicators.note: only every other letter of the two words is used, the rest skipped

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are kept

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a prince to act bravely now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic poetry tells of heroes, so epic serves as an adjective for grand, heroic deeds.

clue.text: Shave around day's start for father

indicators.note: the word for shave goes around the single letter

parts.note: to pare is to shave or trim thinly

indicators.note: the start of the word day is its opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A man shaves at the beginning of each day before becoming a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is an informal term for a chaplain or priest, who is addressed as Father.

clue.text: Familiar rascal periodically found in nunnery

indicators.note: the letters from rascal are discovered inside the word for nunnery

parts.note: a nunnery is a convent

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals, the first, third and fifth of rascal

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters are the ones kept

explanation.surface: A well-known rogue is sometimes discovered hiding in a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversant with something means acquainted with it, a synonym of familiar.

clue.text: Physical work escalates inside pen

indicators.note: the reversed letters go within the word for pen

parts.note: a corral is a pen for livestock

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Physical labour builds up inside a prison pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal punishment is bodily punishment, so the word is an adjective for the body.

clue.text: Greek character melodiously articulates thoughts

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to voice words melodiously is to sing them

explanation.surface: A character from Greece voices their reflections musically.
explanation.definitionFit: Musings are reflections or daydreams, a synonym of thoughts.

clue.text: Trudged from bar haunt after time

indicators.note: the bar and haunt words come after the letter for time

parts.note: a rod is a bar
a den is a favourite haunt

explanation.surface: Someone trudged away from a pub, a favourite haunt, after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; here it is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden is the past participle of tread, walked on, as trudged is of trudge.

clue.text: This should get people going!

definitions.meaning: the clue presents itself as something with a purpose, a remedy
seems to mean motivate or energise; read the other way it means make people visit the lavatory

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a rallying call; the real sense is bodily, relieving constipation.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that loosens the bowels is taken precisely to make someone go to the toilet.

clue.text: Bit of silence for the audience

indicators.note: what listeners hear, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: peace is quiet or silence

explanation.surface: A short pause in a performance for the benefit of the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment, synonymous with a bit.

clue.text: Supporter with complaint about new player

indicators.note: the word for complaint wraps around the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is a grievance
an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: A sponsor complains about a newcomer in the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help, a patron who backs a cause.

clue.text: Recluse before old power, reportedly

parts.note: ere is the archaic word for before

indicators.note: as heard, so the word for power is spelt by its sound

parts.note: might is power or strength

explanation.surface: A hermit who lived before some ancient power, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, especially a Christian one living alone for religious reasons.

clue.text: Overwhelm single sister? Go steady!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun is a religious sister
to date someone is to go out with them regularly

explanation.surface: Someone urges an unattached sister to take up a steady relationship, swamping her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single sister' looks like a lone woman; it splits into one and a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood, figuratively to swamp someone with too much.

clue.text: Beefy things taking runs, naked runs

indicators.note: the word for beefy things takes in the letter for runs

parts.note: steaks are cuts of beef
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Muscular people taking a jog, then dashing about without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beefy' suggests brawny people; it is meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaking is running naked through a public place, so streaks are such dashes.

clue.text: Against help with sweetheart suppressing desires

indicators.note: to suppress here is to hold down inside, so the desires go within

parts.note: aid is help
longs is a verb for desires
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet

explanation.surface: Opposed to help from a lover who stifles their own yearnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the classic split: the heart of sweet is its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside and against both mean beside or close up next to something, as a ship lies against a quay.

clue.text: Hospital department system includes small charge

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: the routine word holds the letter for small inside it

parts.note: a rut is a fixed routine or set way of doing things

explanation.surface: A hospital department's billing system adds a minor fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee; it is the verb, to give someone responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to entrust it to them, a verb of handing over responsibility.

clue.text: Dainty, oddly dulcet strum

parts.note: twee is quaintly dainty, a British word for overly sweet or cute

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth, are taken

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters are the ones kept

explanation.surface: A delicate, sweet-sounding strumming of an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweedle is to play an instrument idly or casually, much like strumming.

clue.text: Belly could be advantage eating everything

indicators.note: the word for advantage consumes the other, so that word sits inside it

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or advantage
all is everything

explanation.surface: A paunch might be an advantage for someone who eats everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belly' is the verb, to swell outward, as a sail bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell out, which is what to belly means as a verb.

clue.text: One hits balls tackling large fighter

indicators.note: the batter grapples with the letter for large, holding it inside

parts.note: a batter is one who hits the ball in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A striker in a game takes on a big opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A battler is a combative person who fights hard, a fighter.

clue.text: Prize fight consumed by publicity

indicators.note: the word for fight is swallowed up, so it sits inside the other

parts.note: an ad is publicity
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A prize fight is drowned in media hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize fight' reads as boxing; 'Prize' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of achievement.

clue.text: Girl caught inside a tale

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes within the other letters

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a made-up story
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl is trapped in a story, as in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a girl's given name, the heroine of Carroll's stories.

clue.text: Caught by dearest, ran, getting divorce

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run spans the end of dearest, all of ran and the start of getting

explanation.surface: A partner discovered by their beloved fled, prompting a divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or separate people, as a divorce separates a couple.

clue.text: Violin top concealing dull interior

indicators.note: the word for top hides the other within it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for 1
mat is a variant spelling of matt, lacking shine

explanation.surface: A violin's upper surface hides a lacklustre inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' just underlines that the dull part sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, as a Strad is by Stradivari.

clue.text: Starts to appear geriatric, exhibiting senility?

definitions.text: Starts to appear geriatric, exhibiting senility?

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.note: the four words supply their opening letters in order

explanation.surface: Someone is beginning to look elderly and show signs of dotage.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes it: someone growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow old, beginning to look elderly and become frail.

clue.text: It isn't commonly journalist being corrupted

parts.note: t'ain't is a colloquial contraction of it isn't
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist corrupted, speaking in common slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tainted is contaminated or morally spoilt, a synonym of corrupted.

clue.text: Revealing the French monarch accepting answer

indicators.note: the French article and king take the letter for answer between them

parts.note: le is French for the
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A French king is shown up on accepting a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaking information is letting it out, disclosing secrets, which is revealing.

clue.text: Queen appearance money backed rock band?

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: the fee word is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a fee is money paid to appear

explanation.surface: Queen, the rock band, are paid an appearance fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' and 'rock band' suggest the group; the definition is a ridge of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral just under the sea, literally a band of rock.

clue.text: Gouache art, in essence, embodying strength

indicators.note: the phrase contains the answer within its body, across the word breaks

parts.note: the run starts at the end of gouache and stops partway into essence

explanation.surface: Watercolour painting at its core embodies vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is vigour and robust health, a synonym of strength.
